sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.3% a year from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].
FY2019 was the break: operating income fell 58.9% [D97] on an $8.3 billion pre-tax Shave Care impairment charge [X112][P62].
FY2020 reversed it, with operating income up 186.2% [D148] as $8.3 billion of the increase was the base-period impairment charge [P71].
Since then the shape is slow compounding: revenue grew 2.0% a year over FY2023 to FY2026 [D664] and operating margin held near its 22.1% median [F30][D648].
The US was the engine for most of the window, contributing 4.0pp of FY2020 growth [D518] and 2.2pp in FY2024 [D530].
In FY2026 the mix flipped: Non-US contributed 3.1pp of the 3.3% growth [D511][D457] while the US added 0.1pp [D536].
FY2026 net sales rose 3% on favorable foreign exchange of 2% and pricing of 1%, with unit volume and mix unchanged [P26].
Fabric & Home Care is the largest segment at 34.8% of revenue [D541], but it added only 0.8pp of FY2026 growth [D543].
Operating income grew slower than revenue in FY2026, falling 3.4% [D458] against 3.3% revenue growth [D457], and EPS rose 1.7% [D461] as the diluted count fell 1.3% [D476].
FY2026 operating margin of 22.7% [F30] sits just above the 22.1% window median [D648] and well below the 24.3% FY2025 high [D647].

The 1.6pp margin decline [D470] came from gross margin and marketing: cost of revenue took 1.0pp [D483] and SG&A 0.6pp [D485], as gross margin fell on unfavorable category mix and SG&A rose on marketing spending [P25].
The largest move was FY2019, when the 11.9pp drop [D109] was almost entirely the 12.1pp residual from the impairment charge [D125].
Net margin of 18.4% [F50] trails operating margin by 4.3pp [D693], narrowed by $1.1 billion of other non-operating income from the Glad joint-venture dissolution gain [X108][P24].
Even so, the operating margin ranks in the 80th percentile against staples peers whose median is 14.3% [D668][D669].
Operating cash flow of $19.6 billion [F80] was 1.22x net income [D444], near the 1.25x window median [D683], and free cash flow was $15.1 billion, a 17.4% margin [F100][D441].
The 9.8% operating cash flow increase [D462] came as net earnings adjusted for non-cash items generated about $19.5 billion, while inventories consumed $641 million on higher safety stock [P3].
Capex rose 16.9% to $4.4 billion [D464][F90], lifting capex to 5.1% of revenue [D440] and 1.40x D&A [D446], the highest capital intensity in the window.
Investing used $4.6 billion, primarily capital expenditures and hedge settlements, partly offset by Glad dissolution proceeds [P2].

The company runs net debt of $24.2 billion [D450], or 27.8% of revenue [D451], a smaller net debt burden than the staples peer median of 32.3% of revenue [D695], ranking in the 67th percentile of three peers [D694].
Long-term debt fell 8.6% to $22.8 billion [F190][D468] while cash rose 4.0% to $9.9 billion [F140][D466], and the current ratio is 0.68x [F180].
Buybacks of $5.0 billion plus dividends of $10.2 billion [X134][X144] equaled 100.7% of free cash flow [D453], and the diluted share count fell 1.3% [D476].
Return on average equity of 30.1% [D456] trails the staples peer median of 44.4% [D681], ranking in the 33rd percentile [D680].

The current ratio has been below 1.0x every year of the window and is 0.68x in FY2026 [F180], but this is structural for a negative-working-capital consumer staple, with working capital at -$12.5 billion [F170].
Payout exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 and FY2026, at 116.6% and 100.7% [D402][D453], funded partly by drawing on cash and debt rather than by a shortfall in earnings.
Days inventory outstanding has climbed from 52 days in FY2017 to 69 days in FY2026 [D21][D455], with FY2026 inventory growth of 8.2% [D480] outpacing revenue growth of 3.3% [D457].
Operating margin: a print below the 22.1% window median [D648] in the FY2027 10-K would confirm the FY2026 cost pressure, while a return above the 24.3% FY2025 high [D647] would reverse it.
Free cash flow margin: holding at or above the 17.2% window median [D654] would keep payout coverage near the FY2026 100.7% level [D453]; a drop toward the 14.4% FY2017 low [D652] would strain it.
Days inventory outstanding: a further rise above the FY2026 69 days [D455] in the next 10-K would extend the safety-stock build described in the filing [P3].
